nodes.description: Biallelic GJC2 variants remove connexin-47 channel function from oligodendrocytes. Missense, nonsense and frameshift alleles were found in the founding families. Expressed in cell lines, the missense alleles P87S, Y269D and M283T form no functional channels. The recurrent promoter variant c.-167A>G acts upstream of the protein, abolishing a SOX10 binding site and lowering promoter activity.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the gene encoding gap junction protein alpha 12 (connexin 46.6) cause Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease.
evidence.snippet: In three of six families with PMLD, we detected five different GJA12 mutations, including missense, nonsense, and frameshift mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Loss-of-function GJA12/Connexin47 mutations cause Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease.
evidence.snippet: Dual whole-cell patch clamping of transfected Neuro2A cells demonstrated that none of the mutants formed functional channels, in contrast to wild type Cx47.

evidence.reference_title: Disrupted SOX10 regulation of GJC2 transcription causes Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease.
evidence.snippet: Functionally, this mutation completely abolished the SOX10 binding and attenuated GJC2 promoter activity.

nodes.description: The tissue-level lesion: CNS myelin is deficient from the start, seen on MRI as diffuse hypomyelination. In mice the lesion appears as vacuolated myelinated fibres with Cx47 loss alone and as thin or absent sheaths when Cx32 is also removed.

nodes.description: Several PMLD1 missense proteins are retained in the endoplasmic reticulum instead of reaching the plasma membrane. In primary oligodendrocytes, three such mutants activate the unfolded protein response and apoptotic pathways, a toxic gain of function on top of channel loss. The milder SPG44 allele p.I33M traffics normally and activates neither, which is one measured difference between the severe and mild ends of the GJC2 spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease is caused not only by a loss of connexin47 function but also by a hemichannel dysfunction.
evidence.snippet: The mutants T265A and A98G_V99insT were retained in the ER, T398I formed gap junctional plaques at the plasma membrane, and G149S showed both, structures at the plasma membrane and ER localization.

evidence.snippet: NCS were normal in all patients with PMD and indicated mild peripheral neuropathy in only 2 of 10 patients with PMLD.

nodes.description: Oligodendrocytes couple to astrocytes through heterotypic Cx47/Cx43 and Cx32/Cx30 channels. PMLD1 mutants fail to form functional channels with astrocytic Cx43, and a knock-in mouse carrying the orthologue of human M283T loses most glial network coupling in the corpus callosum, as Cx47-null mice do. Loss of this panglial network, rather than of Cx47 protein as such, is the proposed core of the disease.

evidence.snippet: Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease 1 (PMLD1) is a slowly progressive leukodystrophy that typically presents during the neonatal or early-infantile period with nystagmus, commonly associated with hypotonia, delayed acquisition of motor milestones, speech delay, and dysarthria.
Cerebellar signs (gait ataxia, dysmetria, intention tremor, head titubation, and dysdiadochokinesia) frequently manifest during childhood.

Motor impairments can lead to swallowing difficulty and orthopedic complications, including hip dislocation and scoliosis.

nodes.description: Oligodendrocyte connexins take part, with the astrocytic K+ channel Kir4.1, in clearing the K+ released by active axons. Without them, myelin develops vacuoles whose size and number track axonal activity. Shown in mice lacking both oligodendrocyte connexins; how much this contributes in human HLD2 is not established.

evidence.snippet: The size and number of myelin vacuoles was dramatically increased when axonal activity was increased, by either a natural stimulus (eye opening) or pharmacological treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic and physiological evidence that oligodendrocyte gap junctions contribute to spatial buffering of potassium released during neuronal activity.
evidence.snippet: Together, these results implicate oligodendrocytes and their connexins as having critical roles in the buffering of K+ released during neuronal activity.

nodes.description: Not available to patients. A single intracerebral injection of an AAV vector expressing Cx47 from the myelin basic protein promoter, given on postnatal day 10 to Cx32/Cx47 double-knockout mice, restored oligodendrocyte gap-junction coupling, improved motor performance and prolonged survival.

evidence.reference_title: Gene therapy targeting oligodendrocytes provides therapeutic benefit in a leukodystrophy model.
evidence.snippet: Application of this oligodendrocyte-targeted somatic gene therapy at postnatal Day 10 in groups of double knockout mice, a well characterized model of hypomyelinating leukodystrophy-2, resulted in significant improvement in motor performance and coordination at 1 month of age in treated compared to mock-treated mice, as well as prolonged survival.
Hearing loss and optic atrophy are observed in rare cases.

nodes.description: Homozygous variant in the noncoding exon 1 promoter at a SOX10 binding site. A founder variant in families of Pakistani origin, estimated to account for about 29% of reported GJC2-PMLD patients. It is missed by sequencing that covers only the coding exon.

evidence.reference_title: Promoter mutation is a common variant in GJC2-associated Pelizaeus-Merzbacher-like disease.
evidence.snippet: This promoter mutation has only recently been reported in GJC2-PMLD but it has been postulated to affect the binding of the transcription factor SOX10 and appears to be a prevalent mutation, accounting for ~29% of reported patients with GJC2-PMLD.

nodes.description: ER-retained missense allele that forms no functional channels and activates the UPR in primary oligodendrocytes; its mouse orthologue (M282T) is the knock-in model.
